key_insight: This paper moves cross-view object geo-localization beyond simple 2D appearance matching by making geometry a first-class signal. It unifies object localization across ground, drone, and satellite views in a single-stage framework designed for more realistic and diverse scenarios.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of locating an object in a geo-tagged reference image from a different viewpoint, especially when existing methods depend too much on 2D visual similarity and are limited by weak datasets, missing geometric metadata, narrow prompting setups, and non-standard field-of-view imagery.
method: Introduces a large-scale, high-fidelity building dataset with geometric annotations to better support cross-view localization research.
Proposes a unified single-stage framework that incorporates geometry-aware reasoning instead of relying only on appearance matching.
Targets more robust object geo-localization across multiple views and prompt types, improving generalization to real-world settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides a stronger benchmark and a more realistic modeling direction for geospatial vision tasks. It can improve localization robustness in mapping, remote sensing, robotics, and urban perception applications.

paper_title: Beyond 2D Matching: A Unified Single-Stage Framework for Geometry-Aware Cross-View Object Geo-Localization
paper_authors: Liyao Wang, Ruipu Wu, Haojun Xu, Lei Shi, Linjiang Huang
